body:
Resolved so far: the reviewed development landings and source commits are recorded in [the v0.15.0 issue reconciliation](https://github.com/ligon/LSMS_Library/blob/8d7a5e55914e700c69ae1a195f96cc2282b6ce64/slurm_logs/release_landing_2026-10-14/RELEASE_ISSUES.org) (PR #998). This issue remains open for the scope below.

The many-to-many provenance model is implemented and tested: multiple IDs, covered/derived relations, aliases, unknown logical-wave handling and backward-compatible scalar/Boolean behavior. Fixed-catalog replay corrects seven previously false missing results; no country-table hash changes in the 103-table probe.

Remaining scope: a failed backfill lookup whose primary catalog ID is absent/filtered still replaces provenance with UNKNOWN and can discard existing hand-recorded metadata. Successful re-stamps preserve the fields. Decide whether failed resolution should leave the record intact or write a separate review artifact. No broad backfill or new live WB census was run. Do not claim preservation under every failure outcome.

comments.body:
**Ruling (@ligon, 2026-10-18)**, from the framework-backlog decision sheet: On a failed resolution, the backfill leaves the existing record intact and writes a separate review artifact listing what it could not resolve. It never downgrades a recorded id to UNKNOWN.

Scheduled for the overnight 2026-10-18 sweep.

title: Preserve existing provenance when a catalog backfill cannot resolve its source
